item.title: Football Player of the Week is North Hunterdon’s Matt Esposito, Week 8
item.description: The 2026 season might have been a struggle for the North Hunterdon High School football team, but last weekend’s victory over neighborhood rival Voorhees in the 51st annual Milk Can Game is a good way to go into the offseason on a supremely positive note. Senior Matt Esposito led the way in the 21-18 victory, which increased the Lions all-time lead in the series to 36-14-1 and gave them their first victory of the season. Esposito rushed 27 times for 193 yards and the three touchdowns, including two in the second half. He also pitched in five tackles on defense, plus an interception. The senior finishes with 916 yards and nine scores for the season, plus a receiving touchdown, while recording 36 tackles, two interceptions and a forced fumble in the Lions’ defensive secondary. “Matt had a tremendous year and was an instrumental piece to the team,” North Hunterdon coach CJ Robinson said. “He brings the effort, attitude, and toughness on Friday nights. His performance last week is a great reflection of the work and commitment he’s put in this year. To see him play at that level and help lead our team to a win was special. We were fortunate to have had him as part of our program.” Simeon Pincus has covered NJ sports since 1997. He can be reached at SPincus@GannettNJ.com . item.title: Horseheads girls, Vestal boys roll in Section 4 Class AA soccer finals
item.description: The Horseheads girls and Vestal boys secured Section 4 Class AA soccer titles in comfortable fashion Thursday, Oct. 29 at Waverly Memorial Stadium. Horseheads earned its third straight sectional title in the first game of the doubleheader, topping Union-Endicott by a 3-0 margin. Vestal's boys pulled away for a 5-1 victory over Horseheads after leading 2-1 at halftime. More: Matchups and scores for the 2026 Section 4 girls soccer tournaments More: Scores and matchups for the 2026 Section 4 boys soccer tournaments Trio of players scored for Horseheads girls Ashley Giammichele, Maddie Ribble, and Sonya Dordoni scored goals for Horseheads as the Blue Raiders punched their ticket into the New York State Public High School Athletic Association tournament. Giammichele added an assist. Giammichele's goal off a corner kick gave Horseheads a 1-0 lead with 18:46 remaining in the first half. Amaya Abeyaratne recorded the assist. Ribble's goal with 29:30 remaining increased the advantage to two goals. Dordoni made it 3-0 with 25:23 to play on a score on a play started by a Sydney Blunt corner kick. Up next : Horseheads (10-4-2) will play a Section 11 foe in a regional final/state quarterfinal Nov. 7 at Chenango Valley High School. Vestal sealed title with strong second half After Tyler Burgin and Isaac Rittenburg scored first-half goals for Vestal, the Golden Bears tacked on three scores in the second half. Rittenburg's second goal was followed by scores from Chase Fundus and Elsan Toric. Dominic Wood scored off an Owen Bachert corner kick with 15 seconds left in the first half to pull Horseheads (6-5-2) within 2-1. Up next : Vestal (10-3) will meet a team from Section 11 in a regional final/state quarterfinal Saturday, Nov. 7 at Chenango Valley High School. item.title: Matchroom's Hearn expected to up Prem influence
item.description: Boxing promoter Eddie Hearn has signed British and Irish Lions Finn Russell and Henry Pollock [PA Media] Renowned boxing promoter Eddie Hearn is expected to ramp up his influence in rugby union after meeting with Prem bosses in Monaco last week. Hearn, who runs Matchroom Sport, has made a foray into rugby by signing high-profile players Finn Russell and Henry Pollock to his stable. And the sports mogul has been backed to make a big impact in the sport by senior figures in the English game. "[Matchroom] will be a force for good. [Hearn] sees that rugby is on a great trajectory and he's very pro the Prem," said Prem Rugby chief executive Simon Massie-Taylor. "I think his ambition goes beyond just representing top athletes. "He doesn't want to be a disruptor. He wants to work with the league, but he definitely wants to agitate for more growth and sees a lot of potential." Hearn has spoken previously of his desire to "turbo-charge" the profile of rugby union and its players, adding it would be a "stroll in the park" to transform the sport. "I'd expect him to represent some more of the top stars in the Prem," said Massie-Taylor. "And so you start to move into other options, whether that's around events, big games, or something specifically commercial around the players across the league. "I don't think he's there to buy a rugby club, but he could definitely help introduce people to it and partner with that." Clubs in profit 'in next five years' Massie-Taylor was speaking around the release of the Prem's second annual financial monitoring report, which revealed that all 10 clubs have passed the financial standards for the 2026/2027 season. Following the demise of London Irish, Wasps and Worcester, the Prem has tightened up its rules with clubs now required to be more transparent over the state of their finances. According to the report the financial picture has improved across the league, with revenues up and club losses forecast to reduce by £26.7m, while Newcastle Red Bulls, Exeter Chiefs and Bath Rugby have all secured major external investment over the past 12 months. However no club is yet in profit, with Saracens and Sale reporting the heaviest losses. "In the next five years we would expect the vast majority of clubs to move into the black," said Massie-Taylor. "And for those that don't the losses would be relatively marginal. But I think there will be a situation when clubs move into a more sustainable position, there will be a desire to re-invest. "So as long as the asset is growing quicker than the aggregate losses, then you have value." 'We are looking to develop English clubs' The report reiterates the plan for the Prem to increase from 10 to 12 teams by the 2030/31 season, with expression of interests to be completed in the coming months. item.title: Commentary: Brewers’ World Series win reminds us what Wisconsin can be
item.description: The World Series game four watch party at American Family Field sold out, with fans packing into the stands along the first and third base sides. (Photo by Henry Redman/Wisconsin Examiner) We don’t have a sports section at the Wisconsin Examiner. But when the Milwaukee Brewers went to the World Series for the first time in 44 years, we couldn’t ignore it. Fortunately, the one member of our staff with a sports reporting background, Henry Redman — the sports editor of his college newspaper at Loyola University Chicago— was willing to drive down to Milwaukee to claim a press box seat at American Family Field. Redman covered game four , watching the big screen with the sold-out crowd of Brewers fans who were ready to cheer a historic Series win as their team played in St. Petersburg. It turned out to be a long night, with the Brewers losing at the bottom of the 12th inning. The next night it fell to reporter Baylor Spears, who has plenty of experience covering late-night legislative hearings, to write up game five , and the Brewers’ first-ever World Series win. The World Series was a welcome break from the divisive politics of this edgy midterm election season. Every resident of our 50-50 purple state was united in rooting for the Brewers. (Well, almost everyone; Spears reports that the latest Marquette poll found 1% of state residents actively rooting against the home team.) As Spears and Redman write, “The team, and its huge win, represents a point of unity.” That feeling, of coming together as a community in a moment of shared civic pride, is a welcome reminder that toxic partisanship is not the only possible atmosphere we can live in. As Milwaukee resident from Brookfield Sarah Coleman told Redman while watching game four, “It says a lot that a small market team swept the highest paid team in Major League Baseball. It’s cool to talk about the underdog.” The Brewers beat the Los Angeles Dodgers in four games out of four in the National League Championship. The Dodgers’ payroll , the highest in Major League Baseball, is two and half times the size of the younger, scrappier Brewers’. Go Brewers! “It’s nice to enjoy something so positive,” Chrystal Glynn-Skipini told Redman. That positivity had an effect on our state’s sour and fractious politics. It lightened voters’ mood and made them less angry, and gave everyone a breather in the heat of a contentious election. It made it harder for Republicans to run their usual play, bashing Milwaukee, the heavily Democratic city President Donald Trump has called “ horrible ” and generations of Republican lawmakers have portrayed in thinly veiled racist terms as a crime-ridden hell hole. Trump declared last week that “ nobody cares ” about a World Series featuring two small-market teams. But here in Wisconsin, Republican gubernatorial candidate Tom Tiffany was savvy enough to celebrate the Brewers’ win, separating it from the barrage of negative ads targeting his rival Milwaukee County Executive David Crowley.

item.title: Revisiting Ohio State's 2014 national title run with Cardale Jones after J.T. Barrett injury
item.description: Revisiting Ohio State's 2014 national title run with Cardale Jones after J.T. Barrett injury originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . Cardale Jones will forever be remembered in Columbus. In 2014, Jones emerged as a cult hero at Ohio State. He started fall camp as a third-string quarterback that year. Braxton Miller went down with a season-ending shoulder injury before the season started, and JT Barrett suffered a fractured ankle in the regular-season finale against Ohio State. In stepped Jones for the Buckeyes – who finished 11-1 in the regular season – and led a national championship run that included victories against Wisconsin in the Big Ten championship game and No. 1 Alabama and No. 3 Oregon in the first four-team College Football Playoff. So, his advice for the quarterback situation at Ohio State is valuable. "If you've got two quarterbacks, you've got none," Jones said on "The Script" podcast this week . "If I'm Ryan Day and I'm on this offensive staff, I'm making sure whoever I let go out there and be the starting quarterback feel like we are gonna win or lose with this guy." Ohio State coach Ryan Day has not named a starting quarterback between Luke Fahey and Tavien St. Clair for Saturday's matchup against USC at the Los Angeles Memorial Coliseum. The Buckeyes lost starting quarterback Julian Sayin – a Heisman Trophy finalist in 2025 – who suffered a right arm injury in the 19-15 victory against Indiana on Oct. 17. Day, however, has used Jones as a point of reference for those quarterbacks. "I shared with them and shared with the team the story of when we won a national championship here with Cardale being the third-string quarterback," Day said in a press conference on Oct. 20 . "So it's been done before. That's a challenge to them, but it's also a challenge to the entire team." MORE: Which unbeaten loses first, Utah, Miami or UCLA? Cardale Jones led Ohio State national title run in 2014 There are similarities to 2014. Barrett finished fifth in the Heisman Trophy voting that season despite the injury against the Wolverines. He had 2,834 passing yards, 938 rushing yards and 45 total TDs that season. Jones – a 6-foot-5, 250-pound quarterback – brought a different skill set to the field. In an interview with Eleven Warriors this week, Jones credited coach Urban Meyer and offensive coordinator Tom Herman for tailoring his skillet to the offense. "I think it just took the guys around me upping their play," Jones told Eleven Warriors . "I think the talent or the confidence was never an issue for me, personally. My coaches may think differently, but I think just coming into a situation where I felt as comfortable as possible with the talent around me." item.title: How will Barcelona line up against Alavés?
item.description: Photo by David Ramos - UEFA/UEFA via Getty Images Barcelona look to bounce back from their first league defeat of the season and maintain their narrow lead at the top of the La Liga table as the leaders welcome a solid Deportivo Alavés side to Camp Nou. Here’s how we think Hansi Flick will line up his troops for Saturday’s battle: Defense The injuries continue to mount after El Clásico and there are two huge games next week against Aston Villa and Atlético Madrid to think about, so it’s pretty much impossible to figure out Flick’s lineup for this one. This is our best guess (and maybe some wishful thinking), but we’ll likely be very wrong. There’s been talk of giving a full debut to young midfielder Brian Fariñas , who played a good portion of preseason at right-back and could be picked as Xavi Espart’s replacement since Jules Kounde is still not ready to return from an ankle injury. Alejandro Balde is expected to remain at left-back after a strong display in El Clásico to give João Cancelo a rest ahead of next week, but Pau Cubarsí and Gerard Martín must start as the only healthy center-backs in the squad for this one. Midfield This will be Flick’s only chance to rest his best players after a marathon of matches and with two other crucial games ahead, so we think the coach will take the chance to rotate in midfield and start all three of Marc Bernal , Frenkie de Jong and Gavi in this one to give Rodri, Pedri and Fermín López a breather. Attack We are also expecting changes up front to save Lamine Yamal and Raphinha’s legs for Tuesday, so we think Karim Adeyemi and Gabriel Jesus will start alongside Anthony Gordon in the attacking trio. item.title: Werder Bremen vs Hoffenheim preview: Two in-form teams face off
item.description: Werder Bremen vs Hoffenheim preview: Two in-form teams face off Werder Bremen It’s been a wild season so far for Werder Bremen, and this past week was a prime example of that. It began on Saturday afternoon. They travelled to Mainz, which is a tough fixture for any Bundesliga side. Fortunately for Bremen the opposition were in a kind mood, gifting them two penalties in the first 25 minutes. Niclas Füllkrug was happy to accept, slotting both home to continue his remarkable goalscoring form. The hosts did pull one back before the break, as Anthony Caci headed home a lovely cross from Sheraldo Becker. They kept attacking and pushing forward in search of an equalizer, but it was Werder who struck next. A lovely counter-attack set up Ludovit Reis, and even though his effort seemed destined for the corner anyway, a deflection guaranteed that it went in. Caci turned from scorer to provider two minutes later, picking out Jae-Sung Lee who then found the bottom corner with a superb headed finish. Mainz had plenty of time left, but the chances dried up, so the win and all three points when to the visitors. Bremen then had another tough road test in the DFB Pokal, unfortunately drawn against Borussia Dortmund in just the 2nd round. It seemed like it was going to be a rout early on, with the favorites jumping out to a 2-0 lead in only 17 minutes. They easily could’ve sealed the result in the opening stages. They didn’t, and Werder made them pay. Füllkrug was subbed on in the 59th minute, and five minutes later he had scored a stunning brace. Another penalty started things off, and then a nutmeg in midfield led to a run up the field and a powering finish that curved away from the goalkeeper and into the back of the net. The contest turned into a classic, and just as it seemed like we were all headed for overtime, Dortmund struck. Goalkeeper Karl Hein was caught out, with Marcel Sabitzer rifling a free-kick from distance that flew past the keeper before he could track back in time. While it was a bitter end for Bremen, it still counted as yet another comeback, showcasing the team’s incredible resolve and attacking ability. They do know that they have to work on the other side of the pitch, as continuing to leak goals at this rate will cost them eventually. The issue with this contest is that they're up against a bogey team of theirs. They haven't won at home to Hoffenheim since 2017, and some supporters, especially my own father, are desperate to see that run end. The Green-White’s are dreaming of Europe, and a win this time around would be a big step in making that dream a reality. item.title: Julian Ward makes decision over deal for £50m Spanish forward after latest twist
item.description: Julian Ward makes decision over deal for £50m Spanish forward after latest twist Liverpool added plenty of forward talent in the summer transfer window. Deals were done for both Victor Munoz and Bradley Barcola. Munoz, 23, came in from Osasuna for around £34m after the Spain FIFA World Cup winner’s release clause was triggered. Barcola meanwhile came on board for around £123m after the Reds successfully concluded negotiations with Paris Saint-Germain. And while those two players represent great signings for now and the future the moves left Andoni Iraola short a right winger. He is having to make do with Cody Gakpo, Rio Ngumoha, Munoz, Barcola, Lewis Koumas and others in the position once occupied by Mohamed Salah. No moves could successfully be concluded over summer for Yankuba Minteh or Ismaila Sarr - meaning Liverpool are still on the lookout for a right-sided option. LFC wanted Otorbi at £25m, won't pay £50m In recent weeks their chase has led them to Valencia - where 19-year-old David Otorbi is catching the eye. The young Spaniard has made a decisive breakthrough for his hometown club this season - enjoying a stellar La Liga rise. With a release clause in his contract standing at €30m (£25m) this was a deal that sporting director Julian Ward was willing to do according to Tribuna Deportivo. Nonetheless Los Che have moved to renew their attacking prospect’s contract until 2031 - DOUBLING his release clause to €60m (£50m) in the process. And according to Fichajes that move - which included a salary increase - has put Liverpool’s chase at an end. While the 2024/25 Premier League champions were willing to do an opportunistic deal at £25m it would appear as though £50m is a little too rich for their bones - even with a lack of options on the right. David Otorbi: Situation summary David Otorbi is a 19-year-old, right-footed winger who primarily operates on Valencia’s right flank. His game centres on pace, direct running and taking defenders on, attacking the outside to deliver crosses and cutbacks. He has broken into Valencia’s first-team rotation this season, scoring his first senior goal against Racing Santander. However, a thigh injury against Villarreal has interrupted his progress, with Spanish reports anticipating at least six weeks out. Valencia have moved to secure him until June 2031 by activating an existing extension early. His release clause reportedly doubles from €30million to €60million, significantly strengthening their negotiating position. Liverpool and Newcastle have been linked, while his agent has confirmed Premier League enquiries. England looks a plausible longer-term destination, but his camp prioritises development at Valencia; an imminent departure is far from assured.

item.title: Time to invest in Bournemouth? - FPL gameweek nine dilemmas
item.description: [Getty Images] BBC Sport's Fantasy Premier League expert FPL Heisenberg gives his answers to some of the biggest dilemmas facing managers heading into gameweek nine. Is now the time to invest in Bournemouth assets? Yes, I think so. They face Leeds at home in gameweek nine, followed by a very appealing run of fixtures over the next few gameweeks. Marcus Tavernier (£6.4m) is my favourite pick. He's been attracting plenty of attention after recent performances and offers a good combination of goal threat and creativity from midfield. Evanilson (£6.2m) is another one I'd consider. He's a decent budget forward who should get opportunities to score in this run of fixtures. If you're after a cheaper route into Bournemouth's attack, he's worth a look. Antonio Silva (£5.0m) is my defender of choice as he's great for defensive contributions, but I won't be rushing to triple up on the Cherries. Should we be buying Jackson after his double against Man City? Nicolas Jackson (£6.7m) is certainly an interesting option after a strong run of recent form - scoring four in his past four Premier League matches. He looks to be finding his feet at Aston Villa and he's an appealing alternative to some of the other budget forwards in the game. Aston Villa face Fulham at home in gameweek nine, which is the start of a very nice run of fixtures to back him in. My only concern is his minutes. There's a slight risk of him being hooked early, especially with Villa juggling Champions League football and promising young striker Brian Madjo (£5.4m) back from injury. However, with his recent form and price in mind, he's definitely worth considering. Is Haaland still the obvious captain choice? Yes, absolutely. Erling Haaland (£15.7m) remains the standout captaincy option for me, even after Manchester City's first Premier League defeat of the season. He scored again against Aston Villa in gameweek eight and continues to be the player I'd back to deliver the biggest points haul in any given match. item.title: Shock Basel loss dents Djokovic's ATP Finals hopes
item.description: Novak Djokovic is playing in Basel for the first time since 2011 [Getty Images] Novak Djokovic's hopes of making a record 19th appearance at the ATP Finals have been dented by a surprise defeat against Jan-Lennard Struff at the Swiss Indoors in Basel. Playing in the tournament for the first time in 15 years, the 39-year-old lost 6-7 (4-7) 7-5 7-6 (7-5) - the first time he has been beaten by Struff in nine meetings. "I knew I needed to go for it. There was only one way to play it. So, I was very, very happy," said the world number 27. "I knew I had to play my best tennis to have a chance. The last eight times he beat me very, very easily. So, I'm very, very happy and pleased with the performance." The year's top-eight performers qualify for the ATP event in Turin and this result leaves Djokovic - the men's game's record 24-time Grand Slam winner - 11th in the standings. Djokovic admitted he expected to feel "a little rusty" after his win against Frenchman Ugo Humbert on Wednesday, but now faces a fight to make the finals as he is outside the top 10 for the first time since 2018. Rafael Jodar holds the final qualifying spot in ninth place, because number one Jannik Sinner is injured and will not take part. Djokovic is 319 points behind Jodar, although he has the opportunity at the Paris Masters in November to move up the rankings. The Serb is aiming to move ahead of Roger Federer with his 19th appearance at the finals in Turin. He has won the event a record seven times and has missed the past two editions with injury - but the last time he failed to qualify on merit was in 2017, when his season was affected by injury. Alexander Zverev, Carlos Alcaraz and Ben Shelton have their places confirmed for the showpiece event in Italy from 15-22 November, although American Shelton also surprisingly lost in Basel. The top seed lost 6-3 6-7 (4-7) 7-6 (7-1) to Swiss wildcard Jerome Kym, who is ranked 222nd in the world. item.title: 'I was very happy': Smriti Mandhana reveals MS Dhoni's special WhatsApp message after World Cup win
item.description: Smriti Mandhana has revealed that former India captain MS Dhoni personally congratulated her after the Indian women's team lifted their maiden ODI World Cup title in November 2025. Speaking at an event featuring Dhoni, Mandhana recalled receiving a WhatsApp message from the legendary cricketer following India's historic triumph. She admitted that the gesture made her particularly happy, knowing that Dhoni is not someone who uses his phone frequently. “He actually did send me a message after the World Cup win. I know he does not use his phone a lot. I was very happy that he used WhatsApp to congratulate all of us," Mandhana said. Host Harsha Bhogle then asked Mandhana whether she had saved Dhoni's number. “I did have his number," she replied. Dhoni, meanwhile, offered an interesting explanation for choosing Mandhana as the recipient of his message. He revealed that she was the only member of the Indian women's team whose contact number he had saved. “I did not know anyone else’s (number) from the team. I wanted the message to go through. We had just shot (a commercial) before that. I thought, ‘Let me send a message to Smriti’ and I mentioned, ‘Please wish everyone who is part of the team," Dhoni said. India created history on November 2, 2025, defeating South Africa by 52 runs in Navi Mumbai to win their first-ever Women's ODI World Cup. The triumph ended the team's long wait for an ICC title. Batting first in the final, India posted 298/7, with Shafali Verma leading the charge with 87 runs and Deepti Sharma contributing 58. Deepti then delivered with the ball, taking five wickets as South Africa were dismissed for 246 despite a century from Laura Wolvaardt.

item.title: Tottenham star calls Real Madrid captain ‘a beast’ but questions his position: ‘He can do much better in midfield’
item.description: Tottenham star calls Real Madrid captain ‘a beast’ but questions his position: ‘He can do much better in midfield’ Federico Valverde has become one of the central figures in Jose Mourinho’s tactical adjustments at Real Madrid . The Uruguayan’s impressive performances at right-back have strengthened the team, but that raises an important question: are Los Blancos sacrificing one of Europe’s best midfielders for better team balance? Tottenham defender Pedro Porro has weighed in during an interview with Cadena Ser’s El Larguero , praising Valverde’s extraordinary versatility. Pedro Porro full of praise for Federico Valverde The Spanish international was asked about Madrid’s right-back situation and spoke about the Uruguayan international. “Fede Valverde can play wherever you want. He’s a beast, an animal. I love Fede,” Porro said. “I think he can do much better in his natural position. There are few midfielders like him these days. That power, that quality, the way he gets forward, his goalscoring ability,” he added. Porro’s assessment comes at a time when Mourinho has just moved Fede to right-back. The results have improved for Madrid since the switch. Federico Valverde’s move to right-back has benefitted Real Madrid. (Photo by Angel Martinez/Getty Images) Despite having both Denzel Dumfries and Trent Alexander-Arnold in the squad, Mourinho feels the team plays better with Fede at right-back. The captain delivered an excellent performance in Madrid’s 2-1 Clasico victory over Barcelona, despite suffering from a physical issue. His performance against RB Leipzig just before the game was even better. The 28-year-old created three chances, recorded 116 touches and won four tackles while operating at full-back. Mourinho faces an important tactical decision At his best in midfield, Valverde covers enormous distances, drives through opposition lines and arrives around the penalty area with a devastating shot. Those qualities are harder to exploit when his primary responsibility is defending the right flank and offering width. Pedro Porro feels Real Madrid will miss out on Fede Valverde, the midfielder. (Photo by David Ramos/Getty Images) Mourinho’s challenge is not deciding whether Valverde can play right-back. That much is already evident. Instead, the manager has to decide whether the cost of sacrificing Valverde’s midfield qualities is worth having the team play better football. Porro’s comments echo the sentiments of many fans who would love to see their captain playing in midfield. However, the team always comes first, and if Mourinho wants to play Fede at right-back going forward, it remains to be seen how the team fares in the coming weeks.

item.title: Dakar announces Portugal and Morocco as 2027 host destinations
item.description: Motorsport photo The 2027 Dakar Rally has been relocated to Portugal and Morocco, with the war in West Asia preventing Saudi Arabia from hosting the event as originally planned. Having been originally scheduled to begin on New Year’s Day, the 49th edition of Dakar will now run from 7-23 January and traverse two continents, bringing the marathon back to its roots in Europe and Africa. As per the new route, the rally will kick off in Portugal, with the Algarve Stadium serving as the venue for the Prologue. Portugal will also host the first full stage of the event, before the rally moves to Morocco for the remaining nine stages. Competitors will initially head to the south of Morocco, before heading back north and running alongside the Atlantic Ocean. After covering nearly 8000km over two weeks, the rally will conclude in capital Marrakesh. "The relocated 49th edition of the Dakar will meet the sporting standards that have always made it the most demanding rally-raid event,” said Dakar director David Castera . “Despite the short timeframe we have had to work with, we have designed a true Dakar. The ACP (Automóvel Club de Portugal) is supporting us in Portugal, having established its round of the FIA-FIM World Rally-Raid Championship as a cornerstone of the season since 2024. And in Morocco, our expertise across the entire territory, combined with the operational capabilities of our internal teams, allows us to go far beyond the formats previously offered in the country: competitors will discover the Kingdom from one end to the other. “We will explore all its distinctive features through a route of unprecedented scale. Here too, the country's expertise in hosting major international events, as well as the quality of its infrastructure, will be invaluable in enabling us to offer everyone a truly first-class Dakar.” There has been plenty of speculation about Dakar 2027, with questions over whether the rally-raid can proceed as planned in Saudi Arabia amid the on-going conflict in the Middle East. Iran-aligned Houthis recently attacked several key sites in the country, including the international airport in Riyadh, plunging the future of the event in serious doubt. But ASO had been considering back up options for several weeks, with Morocco eventually emerging as the most obvious destination due to its landscape and history in rally-raid. The country already plays host to Rally de Moroc, which is included on the World Rally-Raid Championship calendar and is often seen as a dress rehearsal for Dakar itself. ASO had also been mulling pairing Morocco with a European country, with both Spain and Portugal seen as the most likely destination to start the event before the latter was ultimately selected. This means that Dakar will take place outside of Asia for the first time since 2020, when the rally first moved to Saudi Arabia as part of a multi-year deal.
